subject: Nightwatch: post-cutover validation & stabilization cadence
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ACME Cloud SRE <sre@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Nightwatch: post-cutover validation & stabilization cadence

Team — kicking off the Nightwatch thread for the ACME private deployment that cut over this morning. A few constraints and asks up front so we stay tight: 

- Objective: confirm service stabilization for first 24h and hand off a repeatable cadence to ops.
- Primary risks to watch: KV-cache priming divergence, egress ACL flapping, API tail latency spikes >500ms.
- My ask: Connor, run the KV warmup sequence below and share the CSV. Marissa, coordinate observable check-ins + email template to ACME SRE. Irene, I need a short escalation play (who to page at 2xx alerts).

Attached: nightwatch-runbook-v1.pdf (compact runbook), kv-warmup-checks.csv (template).

Nightwatch KV warmup (high level):
1) Start synthetic warmup at t+15m (see runbook).
2) Ramp synth QPS to steady-state over 10m, preserve headers for routing.
3) Validate KV hit-rate converges to >85% and 95th token latency under 350ms.

I'll be on the bridge through 02:00 PT — ping me directly for escalations.

Hannah
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ACME Cloud SRE <sre@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nightwatch: post-cutover validation & stabilization cadence

On Sat, 20 Feb 2027 at 18:05, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Team — kicking off the Nightwatch thread for the ACME private deployment that cut over this morning.

Thanks — started the KV warmup at 18:20 (attached results will follow). Quick run notes:
- Warmup script executed from redwood-warmers-03 in us-west-2.
- Ramp: 0 -> 150 QPS over 10m, keys sampled from production-like set.
- At 18:30 hit-rate 78%, by 18:40 86%. Token latency p95 trending 320ms.

I captured interim output to kv-warmup-checks.csv and uploaded to the drive folder. No errors surfaced from the runtime but saw two brief transient connection resets to acme-egress-2 at 18:33 — working with ACME SRE to validate.

Connor
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: j.delgado@acmecloud.com <j.delgado@acmecloud.com>

Cc: ACME Cloud SRE <sre@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 19:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nightwatch: post-cutover validation & stabilization cadence

On Sat, Feb 20, 2027 at 6:22 PM Connor O'Brien wrote:
> I captured interim output to kv-warmup-checks.csv and uploaded to the drive folder. No errors surfaced from the runtime but saw two brief transient connection resets to acme-egress-2 at 18:33 — working with ACME SRE to validate.

Connor / Hannah — we see the same brief resets on our side; those were caused by a short NAT gateway reconfiguration during the regional routing refresh at 18:32. We rolled back the routing change at 18:35. Our telemetry does not show any request loss, only TCP resets during the window you observed.

We'll keep monitoring and will flag if anything recurs. Happy to join your bridge if you want real-time correlation.

— Juan Delgado
ACME Cloud SRE
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, j.delgado@acmecloud.com
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 02:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nightwatch: post-cutover validation & stabilization cadence

Quick status update from observability side — pulling the three dashboards Hannah requested: API tail, KV hit-rate, and egress errors. Findings so far:
- API tail (p95): spike at 18:50 to 540ms for ~3m, correlated with a single retry storm from an internal batch job (job-id: batch-refactor-11). We muted that job and p95 returned to ~310ms.
- KV hit-rate: stable at 89% across the fleet after warmup completed at 19:05.
- Egress errors: transient TCP resets tracked to ACME NAT change; no sustained errors.

Next steps I took:
- Created a short email template to ACME SRE for the status handover (drive link).
- Spun up an hourly Nightwatch digest for the next 12 hours to capture regressions; will post to the bridge and the drive folder.

Will follow up with the digest CSVs.

Marissa
Infra Observability Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Cloud SRE <sre@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nightwatch: post-cutover validation & stabilization cadence

Finalizing the ops stabilization play for the handoff later today. Short version to page flow (if any of these fire):

1) Page on-call SRE (primary) + inbox to ops-leads@redwood.com for any p95 API > 500ms sustained >5m OR KV hit-rate < 70% for 3m.
2) If p95 > 750ms or KV < 60% escalate to Hannah and trigger warmup rollback plan A (throttle synthetic injection and revert routing changes).
3) For egress networking faults: page network-oncall and notify ACME SRE; if connection resets persist >10m, open NETOPS-8421 and activate cross-org warroom.

I've attached a compact checklist into the drive link and flagged the top 3 runbook steps inline in the document. If no regressions by 14:00 PT, we close Nightwatch and transition to weekly health checks (Ops cadence: Monday 09:00 PT).

Irene
Head of Production Operations
Redwood Inference
